title: Four ways to live across a border

framing.question: When work, spending, home and participation move at different speeds, what happens to the cities on either side?
framing.notice: Analytical archetypes, not measured population categories. People can fit more than one; their size and overlap are unknown.
framing.display_rule: Equal-size cards and categorical directions only. Arrows show a described configuration, not a measured flow or share.

evidence_tags.label: Official statistics
evidence_tags.meaning: Counts or surveys with a stated population and period; not automatically causal.

evidence_tags.label: Official assessment
evidence_tags.meaning: A government interpretation, distinguished from a measured effect.

evidence_tags.label: Academic study
evidence_tags.meaning: A specific research design and population; findings do not transfer automatically.

evidence_tags.label: Corporate / property case
evidence_tags.meaning: A bounded business or place example, not a citywide estimate.

evidence_tags.label: Exploratory conversations
evidence_tags.meaning: Exploratory themes, not representative frequencies or causal findings.

evidence_tags.label: Question to test
evidence_tags.meaning: A plausible mechanism without a demonstrated outcome.

evidence_tags.label: Evidence gap
evidence_tags.meaning: The reviewed material does not establish the direction or magnitude.

archetypes.title: The weekend user
archetypes.configuration: Lives and works in Hong Kong; spends some leisure time and money in Shenzhen.
archetypes.change: Spending moves before home or work.
archetypes.hk: Some local SMEs face adjustment pressure; family and established relationships may still anchor everyday life.
archetypes.shenzhen: Visitor demand creates opportunities for shops and services.

evidence.text: Hong Kong’s government acknowledged challenges for some SMEs from changed visitor consumption and residents’ increased Mainland spending.
Shenzhen recorded 10.449 million overnight visitor-trips from Hong Kong and Macao combined in 2025, up 26.6%.

archetypes.uncertainty: Tourism figures combine Hong Kong and Macao and exclude day-trippers. Neither source shows that northbound shopping weakens Hong Kong belonging or participation.
archetypes.prompt: What moves north, and what stays rooted in Hong Kong?

archetypes.title: The northbound relocator
archetypes.configuration: Hong Kong origin; moves home and more routines to Shenzhen while keeping Hong Kong ties.
archetypes.change: Home moves, but work, family and long-standing connections may remain split.
archetypes.hk: Work, schooling and established relationships can remain important anchors.
archetypes.shenzhen: Residence creates opportunities for repeated local routines; social embedding is not automatic.

evidence.text: In the 2017 travel survey, 90.8% of trips by Hong Kong residents living in the Mainland originated in Shenzhen; schooling and work were major purposes.
A 2025 official reply recorded 8,486 recipients of specified elderly cash-assistance schemes in Shenzhen.

archetypes.uncertainty: Trip patterns are historical. Welfare recipients are a narrow subgroup, not a count of all relocators. Retirement intentions are not actual moves.
archetypes.prompt: What helps residence become relationships and contribution?

archetypes.title: The cross-border commuter / student
archetypes.configuration: Lives in Shenzhen; works or studies in Hong Kong.
archetypes.change: Economic or educational participation is in Hong Kong while home and family routines remain in Shenzhen.
archetypes.hk: Access to workers and learners can support institutions; employment effects depend on occupation and conditions.
archetypes.shenzhen: Home and family life remain locally anchored while daily access depends on the border.

evidence.text: The September 2024 school survey counted 16,139 cross-boundary students: 388 kindergarten, 2,577 primary and 13,174 secondary.
In 2017, trips by Hong Kong residents living in the Mainland were mainly for schooling (45.4%) or work (19.8%).
At end-2025, the Hospital Authority reported 3,284 nurse vacancies and 36 non-locally trained nurses commencing long-term service under the newer pathways.

archetypes.uncertainty: The nursing example is a bounded shortage case, not Shenzhen-commuter data. No current occupation-by-wage commuter dataset is established here.
archetypes.prompt: Where do wages, time, relationships and community effort go?

archetypes.title: The southbound newcomer
archetypes.configuration: Mainland-origin resident moves to Hong Kong for work, education, family or longer-term residence, retaining Mainland ties.
archetypes.change: Home and work may relocate faster than social networks and routines.
archetypes.hk: Economic participation may precede repeated local relationships and contribution.
archetypes.shenzhen: Proximity may support retained routines, but the role of Shenzhen depends on the person.

evidence.text: 26,714 new applications were approved under the Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals in 2025.

archetypes.uncertainty: Approvals are not a count of settled newcomers. Prior Mainland city is not identified by this figure; do not attribute the inflow to Shenzhen or the GBA.
archetypes.prompt: Does proximity to Shenzhen change life after the move?

matrix.title: What is strengthening, and what remains uncertain?
matrix.subtitle: A qualitative synthesis of the reviewed evidence. These labels are not scores, and do not imply equal evidence strength.

hk.text: Pressure on some local SMEs sits alongside accessibility value and sector-specific workforce needs.
hk.caveat: A rent premium benefits some owners while increasing costs for renters. Imported labour effects cannot be isolated from wider demand changes.

shenzhen.text: Visitor demand supports retail and services, but citywide gains do not show who benefits.
shenzhen.caveat: Tourism data combine Hong Kong and Macao overnight trips. Effects on local rents, small firms and displacement remain unestablished.

hk.text: Family and established ties may anchor home even when spending moves.
hk.caveat: A question to investigate, not a measured citywide trend or a causal claim about shopping.

shenzhen.text: Repeated residence and routines may create connections, but proximity alone does not demonstrate social embedding.
shenzhen.caveat: A question to investigate, not a measured citywide trend or a causal claim about shopping.

hk.text: Cross-boundary infrastructure supports access to work, services and leisure.
hk.caveat: Connectivity and trip volumes do not by themselves establish reliability, fair access or resilience to border disruption.

shenzhen.text: The connected region supports access to Hong Kong institutions and cross-border customers.
shenzhen.caveat: The 2017 survey describes historical usage. Do not read historical purpose shares as current ones.

hk.text: No demonstrated direction for volunteering, local events, mutual help or constructive feedback.
hk.caveat: The reviewed sources do not isolate the effect of cross-border routines from wider social changes.

shenzhen.text: Opportunities for participation need to be distinguished from observed participation by cross-border residents.
shenzhen.caveat: Visible community spaces or activities cannot establish who participates or feels attached.
